# re-lint rules

The rules `re-lint check` (and `scripts/lint_requirements.py`) apply to every requirement row. Rule IDs are stable. When Python is not available, apply this table by hand: read each requirement's `Text` and attributes, and report findings in the same shape (`<file>:<line>: <severity> <rule> <ID>: <message>`).

| Rule | Default | Detects | Example that fires | Fix hint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `weak-word` | error | Vague qualifiers with no measurable meaning | `quickly`, `user-friendly`, `appropriate`, `fast`, `easy`, `flexible`, `robust`, `efficient`, `as soon as possible`, `etc.`, `and/or`, `if possible`, `some`, `various` | Replace with a measurable criterion or a reference to a defined term |
| `universal-quantifier` | warning | Absolute claims that are rarely true and hard to verify | `all`, `every`, `always`, `never`, `none`, `each and every`, `any` (as "every"), `no one`, `nothing`, `everything` | Bound the scope or name the exceptions |
| `passive-voice` | warning | Passive construction with no actor | `is validated`, `shall be stored`, `are notified` without `by <actor>` | Name the actor: `the system shall validate` |
| `nominalization` | info | Process words hiding who does what | `validation of`, `processing`, `management of`, `handling of`, `the creation of` | Use the verb with an actor |
| `incomplete-condition` | error | A condition with no consequence, `IF` without `THEN` in unwanted-behavior form, or `WHEN`/`WHILE`/`WHERE`/`IF` with no `shall`/`should`/`may` | `WHEN the user logs in, the balance` | Complete the EARS pattern |
| `missing-obligation` | error | No `shall`/`should`/`may`/`must` and not a user story (`As a ..., I want ...`) | `The system displays the balance` | Add the obligation verb that matches the binding level |
| `future-tense` | warning | `will` used as the obligation verb | `The system will log every refund` | `will` states a fact; use `shall` if it is required |
| `compound-requirement` | warning | More than one obligation verb, or `and`/`or` joining two actions under one `shall` | `shall export the file and email the user` | Split into one requirement per sentence |
| `open-tbd` | info | `TBD`, `TBC`, `??`, `XXX` in text or attributes | `within TBD ms` | Resolve the open question; keep the ID |
| `duplicate-id` | error | Same ID twice in one register (or across registers in the same run) | two `R-012` rows | Allocate a new ID with `re-lint ids next` |
| `invalid-id` | error | ID not matching the schema pattern | `REQ12` | Use the schema prefix and digits |
| `missing-attribute` | error | A required attribute empty (`schema.attributes.required`) | empty `Source` | Fill it; unknown values are `TBD` with an open question |
| `invalid-enum` | error | Attribute value outside `schema.attributes.enums` | `Type=NFR`, `Priority=high` | Use an allowed value |
| `unregistered-source` | warning | `Source` cites an `S-`/`SH-`/`I-` ID not found in the workspace (only when `sources.csv` / `stakeholders.md` exist) | `S-19` not in `sources.csv` | Register the source with `source-inventory` |
| `register-drift` | warning | A detail register echoes requirement text that differs from `requirements.csv` | `verification.csv` text for R-012 is stale | Copy the current text or drop the echo |

## How the rules apply

- Text rules (`weak-word`, `universal-quantifier`, `passive-voice`, `nominalization`, `incomplete-condition`, `missing-obligation`, `future-tense`, `compound-requirement`, `open-tbd`) run on `Text`; `open-tbd` also checks every attribute.
- Story-form requirements (`As a ..., I want ...`) skip `missing-obligation`, `future-tense` and `passive-voice`.
- Rows with status `withdrawn` or `rejected` only get the structural rules.
- `requirements.csv` is the register. A Markdown table is a register only when its header has every required attribute; other tables are views: rows that echo the register are checked for drift, and rows with an unregistered ID get the text rules only.
- `TBD` is a valid placeholder in any attribute: `open-tbd` reports it (info), never `missing-attribute` or `invalid-enum`. Run `--fail-on info` on a release branch to block on open TBDs.
- Quoted (`"..."`) and backticked spans are not linted as prose.
- In EARS sentences, `universal-quantifier`, `passive-voice` and `compound-requirement` look at the response clause (after the condition), so states such as `WHILE the account is locked` are not reported.
- `passive-voice` ignores passives with a `by <actor>` phrase, relative clauses (`points that were earned`), subordinate conditions (`when the purchase is completed`) and placeholders (`to be confirmed`).
- `IF` written in capitals is the EARS unwanted-behavior keyword and needs `THEN`.
- `any` is reported only where it means "every" (`for any`, `at any time`, `shall accept any`, `Any member ...`), not in conditions (`IF any payment fails`).
- `every` followed by an interval (`every 24 hours`, `every day`) is a frequency, not a universal claim.

## Word lists

Weak words (`weak-word`):

`quickly`, `quick`, `fast`, `user-friendly`, `user friendly`, `easy to use`, `easy`, `easily`, `appropriate`, `appropriately`, `as appropriate`, `flexible`, `robust`, `efficient`, `efficiently`, `adequate`, `adequately`, `as soon as possible`, `asap`, `etc.`, `etc`, `and/or`, `if possible`, `where possible`, `normally`, `sufficient`, `sufficiently`, `state-of-the-art`, `state of the art`, `seamless`, `seamlessly`, `intuitive`, `intuitively`, `minimal`, `optimal`, `optimally`, `reasonable`, `reasonably`, `several`, `some`, `various`, `approximately`, `in a timely manner`, `timely`

Universal quantifiers (`universal-quantifier`), plus `any` where it means "every":

`each and every`, `all`, `every`, `always`, `never`, `none`, `no one`, `nobody`, `nothing`, `everything`, `everyone`, `everybody`

Nominalizations (`nominalization`), reported as `<word> of`, plus `processing`:

`validation`, `verification`, `creation`, `deletion`, `calculation`, `computation`, `management`, `handling`, `generation`, `modification`, `registration`, `cancellation`, `submission`, `execution`, `initialization`, `implementation`, `transmission`, `conversion`, `transformation`, `synchronization`, `aggregation`, `evaluation`, `authorization`, `authentication`, `approval`, `processing`, `retrieval`, `storage`, `removal`, `activation`, `deactivation`, `allocation`, `completion`, `extraction`, `migration`, `reconciliation`, `installation`

## Configuration

In `requirements/schema.json`:

```json
"lint": {
  "disable": ["nominalization"],
  "severity": {"passive-voice": "error", "open-tbd": "off"},
  "extra_weak_words": ["blazing"],
  "allow_words": ["Flexible Spending Account"]
}
```

- `disable`: rules that never run.
- `severity`: per-rule `error`, `warning`, `info` or `off`.
- `extra_weak_words`: more words or phrases for `weak-word`.
- `allow_words`: words or phrases (such as glossary terms) never reported by `weak-word`, `universal-quantifier` or `nominalization`.

On the command line: `--disable RULE[,RULE]`, `--enable RULE[,RULE]` (overrides `lint.disable`), `--fail-on error|warning|info`, `--only-ids R-001,R-002`, `--changed-only origin/main`, `--format text|json|github|sarif`.

Exit codes: `0` clean, `1` findings at or above `--fail-on`, `2` usage, schema or parse error.
